Ele me levou ao meu primeiro jogo de Beisebol (NYYankees) e não entendi nada (continuo sem entender) e a andar num Porsche 911T Targa. Fizeram de mim um cidadão mais consciente. Paul tocava “Maracas From Caracas”, tornou-se intenso jornalista político, com passagem pela CNN. Trying our luck

Against aggressive players, I’m usually not in a hurry to react.

A lot of the time, the instinct is to fight back or “prove” something by showing strength right away.
Instead, I’m thinking about the story my opponent is telling — and the one I’m telling as well.

Bluff-catching, for me, is less about making a big stand and more about staying patient long enough to see if the story still makes sense.

In this spot, when he check-raises the flop, he’s representing something stronger than a hand like KQ. Then, when he checks the turn on what’s basically a blank, even though I have a relatively strong hand, I’m either way ahead or way behind. There isn’t much incentive to bet — if he’s bluffing, he just folds, and if he isn’t, I’m way behind.

So the best way for me to make more money in this pot was to check back, represent something like a middle pair, and give him one more chance to stab at the pot while trying to represent a king.

And of course, spots like this are very player-dependent — and this opponent was clearly capable of taking some unorthodox lines.

I went to this tasty little chic Italian-American restaurant in the West Village with a friend after seeing it on a few lists in the village. It was really nice!

The crab and mortadella dip was super tasty, and we ordered the cheesy frittelle because it was in a special box on the menu (though the waiter said that was just bc it’s like a bread and didn’t fit into any category), but they were also super tasty. 

My friend got the halibut, and I got these lobster triangoli, which were fun and tasty (I was most intrigued by the white vodka sauce bc I like regular vodka sauce). It was nice, and I was okay with there just being a few triangles because I did some aggressive snacking before.

We almost went elsewhere for dessert but then decided to try the crespelle, which I’m happy we did because they were super fun - like little caramelizes crepe rolls. Really yum.

A nice place, and since we were quick we were able to switch our counter reservation to a table, which was nice, and there were some walk-ins available at the counter too.

🇺🇸 Finally made it to @sansabinonyc, a seafood-forward restaurant from the team behind @donangienyc (which I have still yet to visit). The food is good - refined, thoughtful - but not quite the sort of experience you need to battle for in the Resy trenches. Still, if you haven’t been, it’s worth a visit.

What we ordered:
🦀 Crab & mortadella dip 
🐟 Spicy tuna
🐙 Octopus carpaccio
🍝 Pasta alle vongole
🥟 Lobster triangoli

The octopus carpaccio and lobster triangoli were the undeniable stars. The carpaccio has been completely reimagined: not the usual thin slices of raw octopus, but a composed dish layering tender octopus with spicy cured pork over a creamy potato base. An unexpected pairing that somehow works.

The lobster triangoli was full of flavour. The spicy kick running through the filling cut really well through the richness of the sauce. 

The vongole, surprisingly, fell flat. A miss for a dish that’s usually foolproof. You can tell they attempted their own twist, but the sauce leaned overly creamy, and the flavours clashed with the brininess of the clams. The spicy tuna and crab dip were solid, but not particularly memorable; I would’ve enjoyed the crab dip more had it been less dill-forward.

….a solid-ish meal from a duo who has a proven track record (duh from next door). Go if you can snag a table without stress… but you’re not missing a life-altering bite if you don’t. #vibeanddine_nyc

When I opened my new, yet old, broken, oversized  door to let the public into my establishment 4 years ago- I had some idea of what I was also agreeing to open to the world. I was going to be forced to give a part of me to the world so they could scrutinize, examine, compare and try to figure out my reason for taking such a wild leap of faith into such a critical industry. 

What I knew about all of this was, I had a unique and particular set of skills that most would either be curious to learn more about, be intimidated by or turned off. That was the fuel I needed to jump in and execute the plan. What was the plan? I wanted the world to respect my gangsta because there is no competition . I knew I cooked better than most so fuck your fancy establishments, white glove service and garnishes. I wanted the world to feel at home - with  no classism, colorism, or discrimination of any kind.  I didn’t need tuition based training (my grandmother was a beast) or an apron to prove my skills. Because God said, “I sent you equipped and pretty much than overqualified for what they will ask from you. Sow do you.” 

Now here I am faced with the season of DO YOU. Ugh come on God. I want this lil restaurant to appear in multiple cities and countries. I want there to be levels to this shit. I want to  remove myself from this kitchen, and put food on peoples tables in the form of supermarket products. I want cookbooks, to teach people that it’s bigger than this there is a legacy attached - hold that. I want to find my face on the screen teaching people how to say “I love you” through food preparation, good conversation and exploration of mind, body and soul. 

God said today, “You lost plenty of sleep last night because you won’t just say what you want me to do, sow you do you. The time is now sow what you want? Put that in the atmosphere and watch me send it priority express very important mail right to you. No one will be able to stop, it’s already in motion.” 

“I’m waiting, get me out the kitchen -send it God.” Spiritual Temper Tantrum but God understands.  #soulfood #statenisland #henrytha8th #sandyground

@shawnaeshouse in Staten Island was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in 2025. The Sugar Daddy Wings were easily one of the best things I ate all year—and I don’t even like wings! The whole meal was incredible, but my favorite item was the yam cornbread, which is brought out as soon as you arrive.

This place is absolutely worth the trip to Staten Island. The boat ride over was beautiful, with a stunning view of the city. But even more memorable was Shaw-nae’s House itself—a true Staten Island gem. We even met Shaw-nae, the namesake and heart of the restaurant. She was amazing—the epitome of hospitality.

My boyfriend and I were celebrating our six-month anniversary, and she took the time to come over, chat with us about our relationship, and thank us for coming. She’s full of character, warmth, and love—and you can taste that in every bite of her food.

The ribs and fries were delicious, the mac & cheese was to die for, and the collard greens were perfect. Shaw-nae’s House only has about eight tables, and the experience feels like you’re dining in her living room. You can do takeout, but I highly recommend dining in for the full, homey atmosphere.

Reservations are booked out six months in advance—and I already can’t wait to go back. 10/10 experience.

SOOTHR
📍East Village, Nueva York (204 E. 13th St.), a un paso del Lower East Side.
🍴Tailandesa moderna, especializada en fideos y curries.
⭐Reconocimiento: Recomendado por la Guía Michelin desde 2021. En 2025 han renovado la recomendación.
💶Precio medio: 40-50$
📝Valoración:
Soothr, cuyo nombre significa “Receta” en tailandés, es una oda al sabor auténtico del Sudeste Asiático en el corazón del East Village. Con su reconocimiento Michelin sostenido desde 2021, este pequeño templo de la cocina tailandesa ha conquistado a neoyorquinos y viajeros con su equilibrio entre intensidad y elegancia.

El local vibra con el bullicio de las noches del downtown: mesas próximas, luz cálida y aromas que envuelven. Su Khao Soi Nuer, con fideos, curry del norte y ternera tierna, es un bálsamo dorado en los días fríos; el Tom Yum Seafood Hot Pot y el Karee Pu Noodles, con cangrejo y curry, exploran el umbral entre dulzor y fuego. Aquí los sabores no se disimulan: se celebran.

Uno de sus platos más memorables es el Duck Noodles: pechuga de pato caramelizada reposando sobre fideos de huevo secos, bañada en una salsa gravy casera, acompañada de baby gailan al vapor. El pato tiene ese punto de dulzor ahumado que contrasta con la firmeza del gailan y la textura de los noodles secos («dry egg noodles») que mantienen mordida y no se ablandan, una característica que distingue los buenos noodles.

Atendidos con una amabilidad que sorprende, el servicio es rápido, cercano y conocedor. Las raciones son generosas y el picante, bien calibrado. Algunos platos pueden parecer algo dulces o de precio elevado, pero la calidad, el cuidado y la fidelidad al recetario tailandés justifican cada bocado.

Soothr es más que un restaurante: es un refugio sensorial, un recordatorio de que la autenticidad aún tiene lugar en Manhattan. Un destino imprescindible para quienes buscan en un plato algo más que sabor: una historia que reconforta.

History Made in Teaneck! 🖤✂️🍽️

Tonight, I had the absolute honor of attending the ribbon cutting ceremony for Sweet T’s Southern Eatery, owned and operated by Dre Perrin and Tonza Houston.  This is their second location, with their first beloved restaurant rooted in Montclair.

But what makes tonight even more special is that Tonza Houston, part of the dynamic Black couple behind Sweet T’s, is now the first Black woman in Teaneck to own a liquor license. She’s not just serving up Southern cuisine, she’s making history!

This is a proud moment for Teaneck, for Black women, and for Black-owned businesses everywhere. I’m excited for what this means for economic growth, culture, and community right here in our town.

If you haven’t experienced Sweet T’s yet, make your reservation soon. Let’s support this beautiful Black-owned business and celebrate this historic achievement.
